transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hi, I'm Dora. I'm a clinical conversational agent, and I'm here to help you with any questions you might have about your cataract surgery recovery. Do you have any questions for me?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora! Yes, I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can go back to light exercise, such as gardening, one week after surgery. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you, that's helpful. I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes again.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: If you were using any eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it's safe to continue using them, unless you've been told otherwise. Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Great to know, thank you! I'm also feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: It's normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to the new lenses. If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend just wearing sunglasses when you go outside. However, if you have significant pain when it's bright or severe light sensitivity, especially if your eye is also red and painful, we may need to assess this further. Do you have any other questions?
